description: Three-way runtime comparison. Before already includes the earlier router and relationship batching optimizations; after adds request-scoped view configuration, an access subquery and Inter font subsets.

methodology.fixture: One non-admin user owning 50 suspended server records, one node, one nest, one egg, one allocation per server. No Wings calls or running game containers in the measured stacks.
methodology.sharedConfiguration: PHP 8.5, four static FPM workers, OPcache 128 MiB, PHP memory_limit 256 MiB; nginx one worker with gzip level 6; config/route/view caches; one queue worker. Each panel 2 CPU quota cores/1 GiB; each MariaDB 1 core/512 MiB; each Redis 0.5 core/128 MiB. REDIS_CLIENT=phpredis on both. Production mode, debug and telemetry off, no extra addons.
methodology.browser: Headless Chromium, 1440x900, deviceScaleFactor 1, no CPU or network throttling, localhost Docker port forwarding. One warm-up pair discarded; ten measured pairs per panel in alternating order. Cold uses a new context restored from an authenticated session; warm reloads the same page/context. Server/OS caches remain warm. Wait for all 50 server names, then 2 seconds to observe paints. Third-party requests are blocked identically to isolate the local panel; blocked URLs are recorded. FCP/LCP are navigation-to-paint; dashboardReady is measured when all server names exist in DOM, a custom application milestone. Heap is CDP JSHeapUsedSize after an explicit garbage collection; not total browser RAM.
methodology.api: GET /api/client/account and GET /api/client?per_page=50, valid user API key, HTTP/1.1 persistent connections, uncompressed response bodies, concurrency 1/8/16; 10-second closed-loop windows, three repetitions with alternating panel order. Two-second warm-up before each run. No new requests after the window, in-flight requests drained and included in elapsed time. Validate every HTTP status and JSON result. Rate limits raised to 1,000,000/min on both disposable panels. Successes per actual elapsed second, not offered requests per second or a maximum capacity claim.
methodology.memory: cgroup v2 memory.current minus inactive_file, clamped to zero (Docker-style working set). Separately retain raw usage bytes. Ten 1-second-spaced samples per window, three windows each after warm-up, idle and during concurrency-16 server-list load. Each sample records panel, database and Redis, and their sum. Peak is the maximum observed sample, not the kernel high-water mark. No application restarts or forced PHP GC between windows. Browser heap and server working set are different metrics.
methodology.limitations: Single shared Windows/WSL2 workstation; existing unrelated game containers remain running. No CPU pinning, controlled network emulation, TLS, WAN latency, mobile device, endurance test or real-player load. This is a controlled local configuration comparison of pinned distributions, not their default deployment presets or proof of general production capacity.

provenance.sourceNotes: Before uses the existing optimized runtime image; the seven application and router files checked at task start match. After starts from that image and applies candidateFiles and the bundled font subsets. Pterodactyl uses its original pinned image. All three have fresh isolated databases and identical resource limits.
provenance.candidateImageNote: The candidate image was derived from the existing optimized Aquadactyl image. The final request-refresh fix was copied into the running candidate, and its Blade cache was rebuilt, before measurements. candidateFiles checksums describe the served PHP/templates and supersede inherited parent-image patchFiles for those paths. candidate/patch contains the final build inputs. OPcache timestamp validation was enabled.
provenance.methodologyClarification: The original runner text says both panels in two places; this run tested three families with identical settings. New font caching rules were not applied to the common benchmark Nginx configuration.
provenance.note: This compact report retains window summaries. Per-request latency samples and raw memory samples are in the original results.json identified by rawReportSha256.
